entries.en: Joker's waiting for you on the bridge, Commander.
Goodbye, Commander.
After what happened to Jenkins, the crew could use some good news. They'll be glad to hear you're okay.
I never want to see anything bad happen to a fellow marine, Commander. Let's just leave it at that.
I'm not one to hold a grudge. I think we're all looking to put Eden Prime behind us.
Sir, you questioned my competence through the entire mission.
That's fair. Guess I overreacted. I just get a little defensive when someone thinks I can't hold my own.
You didn't. Captain Anderson did. Sir.
I'm glad you're okay, Commander. The crew could use some good news after what happened to Jenkins.
Captain Anderson had me transferred to his command. Must have figured I knew what I was doing.
Captain Anderson had me transferred to his command. I'm just sorry Jenkins had to die for me to get this chance.
I've seen friends die before. Comes with being a marine. But to see my whole unit wiped out...
And you never get used to seeing dead civilians. But things would have been a lot worse if you hadn't shown up.
Thanks, Commander. I have to admit, I was a little worried about being assigned to the Normandy. It's nice when someone makes you feel welcome.
You saved a lot of lives, Commander. It might be hard to keep that in perspective with what happened to Jenkins.
Part of me feels guilty over what happened. If Jenkins was still alive, I might not be here.
Thanks, Commander. That means a lot from you. I've never met anyone who was awarded the Star of Terra.
Held off an entire enemy platoon? Alone? With all due respect, Commander, I think you've got somebody watching over you.
Thanks, Commander. I appreciate that.
That's grim, Commander. I guess I shouldn't be surprised, though. Not after Torfan. That must have been hell.
With all due respect, I'm glad you're on our side.
I won't let the Alliance down, sir.
Do you really believe that, Commander? After what happened to you on Akuze? Are you saying you only survived because of random chance?
With respect, sir, I think you had somebody watching over you.
I don't think it's as simple as that, sir.
Sounds like you're disappointed I survived.
I think we got off on the wrong foot, Williams. Maybe we could start again.
You have a problem with me, Chief?
We'd just lost a man. I didn't know you or your capabilities. It was a bad time to integrate you into the team.
Best way to stop that is to show me you're competent. But I don't remember inviting you to come back to the ship with us.
You're not assigned to this ship.
Things were pretty rough down there. Are you okay?
We couldn't have done it without you, Williams.
Dead marines. Dead colonists. And in the end, we still didn't get that beacon.
Jenkins was a valuable part of this crew.
You're a good soldier, Williams. You belong on the Normandy.
There's nothing special about me, Williams. Anyone would have done the same.
When your number comes up, it's over. His did.
Every time you kill, it gets a little easier.
I did what I had to do. You'd better be willing to do the same.
I survived because I refused to die.
Akuze was a bloodbath. Even now, I don't know how I survived. I guess it just wasn't my time.
I need to go speak with Joker.
You don't sound glad.
I'm sorry if I upset you.
Something wrong?
I overreacted.
That's my prerogative.
Why are you on the Normandy?
How are you holding up?
He'll be missed.
Soldiers die.
I should go.
You helped.
The mission failed.
You earned it.
I just did my job.
You start to enjoy it.
It was necessary.
It wasn't luck.
I was lucky.
I'm sorry if I upset you.
Understood, ma'am.
Understood, sir.
Thanks, Commander.
I think you're going to fit in here just fine, Williams.
Everyone on this ship has to do his or her part, Williams. Remember that.
Thanks, Williams. I needed to hear that. I think you're going to fit in here just fine.
I'm not looking for a shoulder to cry on, Williams. Just stay focused on your job.
How are you holding up?
How are you holding up?
Glad to have you.
Don't disappoint me.
You're right.
Save it.
Hey, Commander.
What do you think, Commander? We won't be staying on Eden Prime too long, will we? I'm itching for some real action!
I sincerely hope you're kidding, Corporal. Your 'real action' usually ends with me patching up crew members in the infirmary.
I know how things work, Commander. I've seen my share of combat, but it's foolish to go looking for trouble.
You could both take a lesson from the captain. He's not afraid of combat, but he knows the value of restraint, too.
Yes, Commander? Is there something you need?
I've served with him for a few tours now. He knows when to let things slide and when to crack the whip.
The crew knows he's seen pretty much anything they'll ever run into. And he cares about the people under his command.
Turians are generally well-respected by the other species. Their fleet has more patrols protecting Citadel space than any other.
They don't always get on well with us, though. Some people find them too rigid. Others still blame them for the First Contact War.
As for Nihlus, I haven't said more than two words to him. He usually only speaks to the captain.
I hope we get a chance to see him in action. I heard Nihlus took down an entire enemy platoon all by himself!
Only what I've heard. Spectre agents work directly for the Citadel Council. They usually work alone or in small groups.
Spectres don't have any official power, though. Basically, they're a shadow organization with a mandate to preserve and protect galactic stability.
Protect it at any cost. Don't forget that part. Spectres operate above the law!
Goodbye, Commander.
Marines are meant to fight. You just fix us up when we're done.
What do you know about Captain Anderson?
What can you tell me about Nihlus?
What do you know about the Spectres?
How do you control agents with unlimited power?
The captain's waiting for me.
Part of the job, Doc.
Captain Anderson
Nihlus
The Spectres
Goodbye.
That's dangerous.
I enlisted right out of med school. Earth always seemed boring to me... too safe, too secure. I figured the colonies were teeming with exotic adventure.
I wanted to travel the stars, tending the wounds of tough soldiers with piercing eyes and sensitive souls. Turns out military life isn't quite as romantic as I'd imagined.
But humanity needs the Alliance if we want to keep expanding through the Traverse, and the Alliance always needs good doctors. So I stayed on to do my part.
Sometimes I think about opening a private practice back on Earth, or maybe taking a position at one of the new med centers out in the colonies.
But there's something special about working on soldiers. If I left the Alliance now, I'd feel like I was abandoning them.
I suppose the Council could revoke the Spectre status of an agent who got out of hand. At that point, Citadel Security Services would take over.
Those C-Sec grunts wouldn't stand a chance. A Spectre's worth twenty ordinary soldiers.
The corporal's confusing romantic legends with reality, Commander.
Spectres usually come from the Council races. Like the turians. We've been trying to get a human accepted into their ranks for years now. So far, it hasn't happened.
They're always getting dropped into impossible situations. Forced to survive unbeatable odds. Just like you on Akuze!
How did you end up serving on an Alliance ship?
Ever think you made the wrong choice?
Why don't we have any of our own people in there?
Personal questions
Any regrets?
There are no human Spectres?
I'd never worked with him before this mission. But he has an impressive service record. Over a dozen special commendations.
Tends to keep to himself, though. Maybe because of the headaches. It's not easy being an L2.
Well, most biotics now use the L3 implants. Lt. Alenko was wired with the old L2 configuration. Sometimes there are complications.
You're lucky, Commander. Your implants use the L3 configuration. Lt. Alenko has the older L2. Far more complications.
How well do you know the lieutenant?
What does that have to do with it?
Kaidan Alenko
An L2?
Hey, Commander! You'd make a good Spectre!
Sorry, Commander. I-- I didn't mean to offend you. I respect what you did there. We all do.
Let's not dwell on the past, Commander. Was there something else you needed?
You're a war hero, right? Held off an entire enemy fleet during the Blitz single-handed. That's the kind of talent the Spectres are looking for.
This is all just wild speculation. The Spectres aren't interested in recruiting humans. No matter how capable.
What you did on Torfan. That's what they're looking for. Success at any cost. Ruthless efficiency. Show no mercy.
No! I didn't mean.... Sorry, Commander. That just came out wrong. I never meant any disrespect.
Fifty marines died there, Jenkins.
I try not to think about Akuze.
I didn't enjoy Torfan. I just did what I had to do.
Sounds like my kind of job.
Show some respect!
Those are bad memories.
I'm not a monster!
I could do that.
The crew's lives are in your hands, Shepard. Try to take good care of them.
I'm glad to see you're feeling better, Commander.
Yes, Commander? Is there something you need?
Severe mental disabilities, insanity, crippling physical pain. There's a long list of horrific side effects. Kaidan's lucky. He just gets migraines.
What kind of complications?
Complications?
It's strange, being a fugitive from the Alliance.
This crew has sacrificed everything for you, Shepard. Don't let us down.
The asari are remarkable, aren't they? Can you believe Liara is twice my age?
Sorry, Doc. But this waiting's killing me. I've never been on a mission like this before. Not one with a Spectre on board!
Sorry, Commander. But this waiting's killing me. I've never been on a mission like this before. Not one with a Spectre on board!
Easy for you to say. You proved yourself on Akuze. Everybody knows what you can do.
Easy for you to say. You proved yourself in the Blitz. Everybody knows what you can do.
Easy for you to say. You proved yourself on Torfan. Everybody knows what you can do.
This is my big chance. I need to show the brass what I can do!
Don't worry, ma'am. I'm not going to screw this up.
Don't worry, sir. I'm not going to screw this up.
It's very peaceful, Commander. They've been real careful with development, so you don't have any city noise or pollution.
My parents lived on the outskirts of the colony. At night, I used to climb this big hill and stare across the fields back at the lights from the main settlement.
It was gorgeous. But when I got older, I realized it was a little too calm and quiet for me. That's why I joined the Alliance. Even paradise gets boring after a while.
Not really sure, Commander. Eden Prime's one of our most stable colonies. Good place to take the Normandy for her shakedown run, I guess. No real danger there.
But there's got to be something else going on. We've got a Spectre on board! That's why I'm so wound up. I can't wait for the real mission to start!
I heard Nihlus once took down an entire enemy platoon all by himself. Man, I can't believe I'm on a mission with an actual Spectre!
The Spectres police themselves. An agent goes rogue, they send another agent to take 'em down. That's Spectre justice!
I should go.
You need to calm down, Corporal. A good soldier stays cool, even under fire.
Only a fool goes looking for a fight, Corporal.
Just treat this like every other assignment you've had and everything will work out.
Do your job, follow my orders, and there won't be any problems.
You're young, Corporal. You have a long career ahead of you. Don't do something stupid to mess it up.
This mission isn't about personal glory, Corporal! We have a job to do. Don't do anything stupid to mess it up!
You're from Eden Prime, aren't you Jenkins? What's it like?
Any idea why Eden Prime was chosen as our destination?
Goodbye.
Relax, Jenkins.
The doctor's right.
You'll do fine.
It's just another mission.
There's no rush.
Be careful.
Don't play the hero!
Eden Prime
Why are we going there?
Spectres sound dangerous.
Spectres sound dangerous.
Spectres sound dangerous.
Spectres sound dangerous.
You probably don't want to keep the captain waiting, Commander.
Joker's waiting for you on the bridge.
Commander. I'm glad to see you're okay. Losing Jenkins was hard on the crew. And I'm glad we didn't lose you, too.
Yeah, you never get used to seeing dead civilians. Doesn't seem right, somehow. But at least you stopped Saren from wiping out the whole colony.
We're marines. We stick together. I'm just sorry we lost Jenkins.
Maybe you're right. Things went bad. Real bad. I still can't believe we lost Jenkins.
I know that. But I don't have to like it.
I was there. You did everything right. It was just bad luck.
Sure thing, Commander.
Glad to see you're okay, Commander.
Things were pretty rough down there.
I couldn't have done it without you.
Dead marines. Dead colonists. And in the end, we still didn't get that beacon.
There's nothing we could have done to save him.
Yeah... I wish I could've done something to save him.
I need to go see Joker.
How are you holding up?
Soldiers die.
Jenkins will be missed.
We'll talk later.
You helped.
The mission failed.
It's been a hell of a shakedown cruise. Our first mission ends with one Spectre killing another.
The Citadel Council's not gonna be happy about that. Probably use it to lever more concessions out of the Alliance.
Yeah. A lot of biotics are. We're not restricted, but we sure don't go undocumented. May as well get a paycheck for it.
Besides, my father served. Made him proud when I enlisted. Eventually. But is that why you're here? Because of your family?
Ah, that's right. Akuze.  I imagine that bought you any post in the fleet.
Ah, that's right. The Blitz. I imagine that bought you any post in the fleet.
Ah, that's right. Torfan. Messy business. I imagine that bought you any post in the fleet.
That how you got here? I heard about Akuze. I bet you had your pick of posts after that.
Is that how you got here? I heard about the Skyllian Blitz. I bet you had your pick of posts after that.
I heard about Torfan. I bet you had your pick of posts after that.
Word is we're heading for the Citadel, ma'am. Can you tell me why?
Makes sense. They'd probably like to know he's not working for them anymore.
Yes, ma'am. Sorry.
Understood, ma'am.
Whatever happens, we'll be ready. Commander.
Five by five, ma'am. Is there anything else before we head ashore?
Absolutely, Commander. Anything else before we head ashore?
An ambassador? I'd just follow standard operational procedure. Salute anything you can't eat or kill.
Good luck, ma'am.
Aye, aye ma'am.
Some of the crew could use it. Commander
You've got a good grasp of the situation. You a career man?
I was a regular Navy brat. I got a little more noteworthy than the folks expected.
I never met my parents. If they wanted to see me, they'd have contacted me after that mess a few years back.
My family were homesteaders on Mindoir. I'm the only one left. But I've moved beyond that.
Couldn't keep me out if you tried. Best way to explore the galaxy is behind a cannon.
The captain hopes the Ambassador can get an audience with the Council. Tell them what Saren's been up to.
If the captain thought you needed to know, he'd tell you.
The captain's briefing was confidential.
We'll talk another time. Make sure you're good to go for this meeting with the ambassador.
There's something big coming. I don't want anyone messing it up. You read me, Lieutenant?
Whatever's going on, the captain can handle it.
Any advice on how to act in front of an ambassador? I don't meet many politicians.
Keep your concerns in check. You don't want to get a rep for questioning orders.
We're headed for the Citadel. When we get done with business, you and I should work out a liberty rotation.
Seems like you've been around.
Keep it to yourself.
Don't worry about it.
Something similar.
I don't have one.
We were farmers.
I'm in it for the action.
It's not important right now.
We want to brief the Council.
Just follow your orders.
I can't say.
You know any protocol?
Just secure your mouth.
No.
